text:
Taylor: Nimbus Data is greenlighting a Private POC this afternoon. They asked for guidance: peering vs PrivateLink, minimal route changes, and DNS. Can we assemble a decision + pasteable snippets for their cloud eng?

Sam: TL;DR: Peering = fastest for POCs if CIDRs don't overlap. PrivateLink = better for stricter routing/enforcement and when customers won't touch route tables. Share both options and a short decision tree.

Ivy: Decision tree (short): 1) Do CIDRs overlap? Yes -> PrivateLink. No -> Go to 2. 2) Can customer update RTBs and resolver rules? Yes -> Peering + Route53 resolver. No -> PrivateLink. 3) Need per-AZ redundancy? Both support it; PrivateLink requires interface endpoints per AZ.

Sam: Minimal peering handoff (pasteable):
```bash
# create peering (customer)
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-cust123 --peer-vpc-id vpc-redwood --peer-owner-id 123456789012
# accept (redwood) -> or customer accepts depending on flow
```
Then RTB updates (customer):
```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-custA --destination-cidr-block 10.210.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-XXX
```
Our side (redwood):
```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-rwdA --destination-cidr-block 10.80.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-XXX
aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-XXX --accepter-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true --requester-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true
```
Replace IDs.

Ivy: For PrivateLink quick handoff: we give them a service name (e.g., com.redwood.vpce.prod) and they create interface endpoints per AZ. Example snippet for customer:
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-cust123 --service-name com.redwood.vpce.prod --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-az1,subnet-az2 --security-group-ids sg-allow-https
```
They must add SG rule to allow outbound HTTPS to the endpoint.

Sam: DNS notes: with peering prefer Route53 resolver inbound rule: customer creates outbound rule forwarding queries for our private zone to our resolver IPs. With PrivateLink they get endpoint DNS names; no resolver required.

Ivy: Security checklist for POC: - Provide customer CIDRs we'll route to. - Require TCP/443 from those CIDRs to our control-plane IPs or peered CIDR. - Do NOT propagate 0.0.0.0/0 into peered RTBs. - If they use NAT/Firewall, ask for EIP(s) so we can whitelist egress origins. - For POC mTLS is optional but recommended for prod; include cert fingerprint in questionnaire if requested.

Taylor: Can someone add a tiny CloudFormation snippet for the route creation I can drop in the ticket?

Sam: Short CF sample for peering route (customer):
```yaml
Resources:
  PeeringRoute:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Route
    Properties:
      RouteTableId: rtb-custA
      DestinationCidrBlock: 10.210.0.0/16
      VpcPeeringConnectionId: pcx-XXX
```

Ivy: infra note: automated deploys will wait until peering/endpoint healthy. net-bot will mark the ticket blocked until connectivity is observed.

net-bot: Action: create ticket S-POC-789 to collect RTB IDs, NAT EIPs, preferred option (peering|privatelink), and whether they want assume-role automation for acceptance.

Taylor: Perfect. I'll send both option snippets and ask for RTB IDs + NAT EIPs. Will update when they reply. :rocket:
